title: The arithmetic is not the arithmetic you wrote

prereqs.why: Every line of the output is one application of the promotion and conversion rules.

statement:
Every line here is **well defined** — there is no undefined behaviour and nothing implementation-specific on a normal 64-bit Linux build where `int` is 32 bits.


**What does it print?** Four lines.
hints: Before any arithmetic, C promotes anything narrower than `int` to `int`. So what are the types of `a` and `b` by the time the `+` happens?
The third line is asking about the *type* of `a + b`, not its value. `sizeof` never evaluates its operand — it only asks what type it would have.
The second line is the famous one. When one operand is `unsigned int` and the other is `int`, which way does the conversion go? Work out what -1 becomes.
